I am extremely disappointed with my experience at PetSmart Grooming. I dropped off my Oreo happy, healthy dog for a routine grooming appointment, and he came home acting like a completely different dog.

Since the grooming, he has refused to eat or drink water on his own, cries constantly, doesn’t want to be touched, and won’t even leave his pillow. He has been acting scared and traumatized. I took him to the veterinarian, who examined him and did not find any visible injuries or cuts, but agreed that his behavior suggests he experienced some type of trauma or extreme stress. It even crossed my mind that he may have been given something without my authorization because his behavior changed so dramatically.

I have no way of knowing what happened after I dropped him off, and that is the most upsetting part. As pet owners, we trust that our dogs will be treated with kindness and compassion when they are left in someone else’s care.

I hope PetSmart takes this matter seriously, investigates what happened during my dog’s appointment, and ensures that no other pet or family has to go through an experience like this.

I'm writing to express my disappointment after a recent experience at one of your PetSmart locations, 4146 S Pulaski Rd, Chicago, IL 60632, on 05/27/2025. I was shopping around for my cat and dog essentials, and my daughter urgently needed to use the restroom. My daughter went to ask a lady with glasses working around the fish aisle, and we were told rudely that the restroom is not for public use and that their policy has been like that for a year already.  This is the first time I've heard that the restrooms are unavailable for customers, and I've been coming to this PetSmart store for more than 5 years now. After this comment, I went up to the register to ask another associate if they could give me the code for the restroom, and they said that the restroom is out of service. Now I'm getting two different answers, and I was forced to rush during my shopping to find a restroom elsewhere.
I hope PetSmart will reconsider its policy on restroom access, particularly for families with children. It's difficult to understand why a family-friendly store that caters to pet owners, many of whom are parents, would not accommodate such a basic need. In my opinion, I feel like basic courtesy and consideration can go a long way in building customer loyalty.

I don’t often leave reviews but I think this place deserves the praise! I have taken my 2 year old cockapoo to 2 dog groomers. The very first groomers I took him to returned him injured and tried to blame it on me. The second grooming place , I almost cried every time they returned him to me (which was only twice). I was recommended by my best friend and sister to try this specific location and THANK GOD! I’ve only ever gone with Luigi, but I’ve never had a bad experience with him. My main concern always is my baby, as long as he’s happy and well taken care of I’m a happy customer. The first time Luigi cut his hair I had gone to the vet days prior because of his allergies and acid reflux, Luigi noticed upon his appointment how that affected his fur and gave me the same recommendation I got from my vet. Today was his second appointment with Luigi and he noticed his paws were matted because of his allergies, he followed up with me and even gave me recommendations to help reduce the licking. My Leo is already on a diet and medication to help his allergies, but the fact that this is the only groomer who pays so much attention to detail is the reason he has gained 2 loyal customers. Leo and I are grateful for Luigi.

Luigi did not even give us a curtesy call after 12:30 (even tho we confirmed at 12:02). Yes we were late, but you have a grace period. DONT KICK US OUT when we make in during grace and tell us at 12:46 “we can no longer help you” (one minute after grace). We take our two dogs here for grooming, and for the amount of money we spend this is not the treatment a customer should get. Will be taking our business elsewhere. Next time dont tell a customer there is a 15 min grace period. Instead, just have Luigi kick them out, problem solved.
